gloss: to read through; to finish reading (a book)

definitions.gloss: to read through; to finish reading (a lengthy or difficult work)
definitions.explanation: To read a book or text from beginning to end, especially one that is long, challenging, or requires effort. Implies accomplishment and perseverance.

examples.japanese: {長編小説|ちょうへんしょうせつ}を{読破|どくは}した。
examples.english: I finished reading a long novel.

examples.japanese: {夏休|なつやす}みに{全巻|ぜんかん}{読破|どくは}を{目指|めざ}す。
examples.english: I aim to read through all the volumes during summer vacation.

examples.japanese: {難解|なんかい}な{哲学書|てつがくしょ}を{三|さん}か{月|げつ}かけて{読破|どくは}した。
examples.english: I spent three months reading through a difficult philosophy book.

notes:
Composed of {読|どく} (read) + {破|は} (break through). The {破|は} element conveys the idea of pushing through to completion, suggesting effort and determination. Used primarily for books, series, or other substantial reading material.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {全巻|ぜんかん}{読破|どくは}: reading through all volumes
- {一気|いっき}に{読破|どくは}する: to read through in one sitting
- {長編|ちょうへん}を{読破|どくは}する: to finish reading a long work
- {読破|どくは}{目標|もくひょう}: reading goal (number of books to finish)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {読了|どくりょう}する: to finish reading — more neutral, simply means reaching the end without the "pushing through" nuance
- {読|よ}み{終|お}える: to finish reading — the plain everyday expression
- {完読|かんどく}する: to read completely — similar but less common
